mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen steadily for three consecutive weeks (-15.4 to -13.6). This momentum reflects accumulating behavioral adaptation to reopening and is expected to persist, pushing the next-28-day mean above the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28 days despite the three-week uptrend, indicating momentum has stalled.

mechanism_narrative: Spain's state-of-alarm restrictions lifted on 2021-05-09, just before this snapshot. In this reopening regime, stabilized WORKPLACES (-13.0 to -12.7) and plateaued TRANSIT (around -35 to -37) indicate loosened mobility constraints that will translate into higher retail footfall over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-05-15 is six days after state-of-alarm expiry
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain stable or improve, implying policy easing did not transmit to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility plunged sharply from -19.7 to -33.9 in the last week. If this drop exceeds a 10-point weekly threshold and persists, it signals substitution away from outdoor leisure toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week and remains below the prior 4-week average
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop exceeding 10 points, or PARKS rebounds immediately without a corresponding retail shift.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in WORKPLACES (toward less negative values) combined with stable or improving TRANSIT indicates resumed commuting patterns that generate ancillary retail trips near transit corridors and office clusters, raising RETAIL_REC over a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves while TRANSIT does not worsen by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -13.4 to -12.1 then -12.7, TRANSIT stayed near -35 to -37
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES improves and TRANSIT stays flat, indicating commuting-driven retail spillover is absent.

mechanism_narrative: As Madrid moves into late spring (mid-May), warmer weather increases outdoor leisure demand captured by PARKS, drawing discretionary time away from retail and recreation venues and suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is mid-May, entering warmer season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days concurrently with rising PARKS mobility, showing no substitution effect between outdoor and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains persistently elevated (around 4.4-4.9) without decline, indicating continued risk-averse, home-centered behavior among residents that caps discretionary retail outings over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed in a narrow 4.4-4.9 band for four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains flat or elevated, disproving the caution-suppression link.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility crossed from negative to positive territory (0.7 then 0.4) in the last two weeks, signaling eased essential-shopping restrictions and normalized errand behavior that typically precedes a broader rebound in retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 and remains positive for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive at t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week after GROCERY_PHARM sustains positive values, indicating no transmission from essential to discretionary mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A mild weekly worsening in TRANSIT (-35.1 to -36.7) combined with continued WORKPLACES stability suggests a shift toward private vehicle use rather than reduced overall mobility; this substitution sustains or slightly boosts retail visits over a two-week horizon as commuters still reach retail destinations by car.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT worsens by more than 1 point week-on-week while WORKPLACES stays within 1 point of prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT worsened from -35.1 to -36.7 while WORKPLACES held near -12 to -13
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT worsening and WORKPLACES remaining stable, indicating no substitution toward private transport is supporting retail visits.
